intro: Istanbul is the only major city on two continents, so you can have breakfast in Europe and lunch in Asia.
facts: Start at Hagia Sophia, built nearly 1,500 years ago as a church, later a mosque, and the largest cathedral on Earth for almost a thousand years.
Across the square, the Blue Mosque glows with more than twenty thousand hand-painted tiles; it is a working mosque, so dress modestly and avoid prayer times.
Get lost in the Grand Bazaar, a covered maze of about four thousand shops trading gold, carpets, ceramics, and lamps since the 1450s.
Take the public commuter ferry across the Bosphorus instead of a tour boat; it costs about a bus fare and lands you in Asia for lunch.
End at Galata Tower for the view, then eat a fish sandwich by the bridge while fishermen line the railings above you.
outro: Save this for your Istanbul trip.
